rationale.consistency: Threads order as a plain param alongside options/warnings/gc and as an unexported Helper field, matching how the package already passes per-adaptation state; parseOptOrder uses existingVal like other fold-together options.
rationale.edge_cases: Multiple order lines chain via existingVal; invalid order returns before any state changes; options map is copied so reuse is safe; buildSubroute/sortRoutes fall back to global order when empty. Silently deleting a caller-supplied options["order"] is an odd, unexplained choice.
rationale.scope: Focused on the order state; slices.Clone of the default order and reordering the arg check in parseOptOrder are small but defensible; no unrelated refactors.
rationale.readability: Names are clear, but the options copy plus delete("order") at the top of Setup has no comment explaining why, and the fallback-to-directiveOrder logic is repeated in Setup, buildSubroute and sortRoutes.
rationale.robustness: No writes to directiveOrder after init, so concurrent adaptations share only immutable state; clone before DeleteFunc avoids aliasing; failure paths leave nothing behind. Caller's options map is no longer populated by Setup, a quiet behaviour change.
rationale.maintainability: Order now has three sources (param, Helper field, global fallback) which future callers must keep aligned; the delete of a specific key from the copied map is hidden coupling. Otherwise the parameter threading is straightforward to extend.
